findings.mechanism: functools.lru_cache(maxsize=None) on the instance method category_totals creates one module-lifetime cache on the function. Its key includes `self`, and ReportService.handle builds a new ReportBuilder per request, so every summary request misses and adds a new entry. The entry pins the builder (and its _columns lists and store reference) plus the result tuple. Nothing is ever evicted.
findings.cause: lru_cache on a method with unbounded maxsize and a per-request instance as part of the key
findings.evidence: Ran load.run in 2000-request batches under tracemalloc with gc.collect between batches. Traced memory went 4.6MB, 9.2MB, 13.8MB, 18.5MB. cache_info showed hits=0 and currsize growing 1600, 3200, 4800, 6400 (one per summary request, i.e. 4 of every 5 requests). That is roughly 2.3KB retained per request, linear and unbounded.
findings.discriminator: hits=0 with currsize equal to misses: the cache never reuses an entry, because each key contains a fresh builder. Fix: cache outside the instance, keyed on (account, month) with a bounded maxsize, or drop the cache and build the ReportBuilder once per service.

findings.mechanism: The per-builder _columns lists are cleared at the start of every render, so they do not grow within a builder.
findings.cause: looked suspicious as a buffer, but it is bounded
findings.evidence: Code reading, plus the tracemalloc batches above. Growth tracked the lru_cache entry count, not the column sizes. Detail requests (1 in 5) are never cached, and their builders are freed.
findings.discriminator: column.clear() runs at the top of render, and detail-request builders are not cached, so they are garbage collected after the response. The _columns lists are only retained when the lru_cache pins the builder (see the first finding).
